title: Hot-corner reveal: long-press gesture, drop 'off', size + hold-time sliders
description:
Follow-up to calvin-hgy (PR #61). Three changes:

1. LONG-PRESS REVEAL (occlusion fix): the 64px corner currently intercepts short taps meant for calendar/photo content underneath. Make the corner visual pointer-events:none (pure hint, keeps keyboard <button>), and detect a configurable long-press by coordinates at the dashboard level (reuse the startRegionResize pointerdown pattern). Short taps fall through to content; press-and-hold in the corner reveals. Suppress the trailing content click via a time-bounded capture-phase listener.

2. DROP 'off': remove the 'off' option from Reveal corner. Opacity 0 already gives invisible-but-active. Persisted 'off' normalizes to bottom-left (removes the lockout footgun).

3. SLIDERS: add hotCornerSize (clamped slider, px) and hotCornerLongPressMs (clamped slider, ms) settings under Display -> Kiosk & touch. New reusable ui/RangeSlider.vue.

Store: config.js + configRegistry.js (hotCornerSize default 64, hotCornerLongPressMs default 500). Overlay: MinimalUIOverlay.vue. Gesture: new composable + Dashboard.vue wiring. Settings: DisplaySettings.vue. Tests + Playwright touch verification.

Short taps fall through to calendar/content. Dropped 'off' (normalizes to bottom-left, kills the lockout footgun; opacity 0 = invisible-but-armed). Added hotCornerSize + hotCornerLongPressMs sliders (new ui/RangeSlider.vue) under Display -> Kiosk & touch. 775 unit tests pass, eslint+prettier clean, build clean. title: FIX: breadcrumb/section indicator updates unreliable across categories
description: Reported 2026-06-29. The E3 topbar section indicator (scroll-spy via IntersectionObserver in Settings.vue) updates unreliably on all categories. Likely root cause: the observer uses the VIEWPORT as root with rootMargin '0px 0px -70% 0px', but after the E3 sticky app-shell the sections scroll inside .settings-content (which starts ~150px below the viewport top, under the fixed topbar+search). The detection band no longer aligns with the content pane, so the 'topmost visible section' pick is flaky (last section may never reach the band; updates lag/skip). Proper fix: set observer root to the .settings-content scroll container and tune rootMargin relative to it (or compute the active section from scrollTop). Use systematic-debugging; verify on-device across Plugins/Content/Device/Maintenance.

Root causes: scroll-spy matched .settings-section (incl. embedded CollapsibleSections without eyebrows) and short trailing sections couldn't reach a top reference line. title: Built-in themes: tint the modern shell + resolve Dark-theme vs dark-mode overlap
description: The built-in themes (Ocean/Forest/Sunset) only recolor the accent on the redesigned shell; a deeper IA smell exists between the 'Dark' theme and dark mode. Two related sub-problems, discovered while fixing the calvin-plugins midnight-theme (added focus + redesign surface tokens; PR pending).
design:
## Background

Theme SELECTION (Light/Dark/Ocean/Forest/Sunset) and light/dark MODE are two
independent systems:

- MODE (`themeMode` in useTheme.js) toggles the `.dark` class on <html>, which
  is what actually drives the redesign surface tokens (`--bg-1`, `--ink`,
  `--line`, …) defined in `frontend/src/styles/theme.css`.
- SELECTION (`selectedThemeId`) layers a theme's `variables` on top via
  `applyCustomTheme()` — writing each key verbatim as `--<key>` on :root.

The built-in themes (`backend/data/themes/builtin.json`) only set the LEGACY
token set (`bg-primary`, `text-primary`, `accent-primary`, calendar-*, …) plus
`focus`. The redesigned UI reads the NEW semantic tokens (`--bg-1`, `--ink`,
`--line`, `--focus`, `--ok/warn/err`) in ~66 files vs ~11 for the legacy set.

## Problem 1 — expressive themes don't tint the modern surfaces (data fix)

Ocean/Forest/Sunset each carry a surface tint in their palette (e.g. Ocean
`bg-primary: #e8f4f8`), but the modern shell reads `--bg-1` which they don't
set. Net effect on the redesigned shell:

- Ocean + light mode  → WHITE surfaces, blue accent (tint ignored)
- Ocean + dark mode   → NEUTRAL dark surfaces (from `.dark`), blue accent

FIX: add the redesign surface tokens to each of Ocean/Forest/Sunset, in BOTH
`variables` and `dark_mode`, mapped from the theme's existing palette:
  bg-1 <- bg-primary, bg-2 <- bg-secondary, bg-0 <- a shade darker,
  ink <- text-primary, ink-2 <- text-secondary, ink-3 <- text-tertiary,
  line <- border-color, line-soft <- a softer divider,
  ok <- accent-secondary, warn <- accent-warning, err <- accent-error.
  (focus already present.)
Leave `light` alone (base; no-op on modern shell is correct).
This is exactly the fix applied to the midnight-theme (theme.json v1.1.0).
Covered by `backend/tests/integration/test_api_themes.py`.

## Problem 2 — "Dark" theme vs dark MODE overlap (design pass)

Selecting the "Dark" THEME (`selectedThemeId='dark'`) does NOT add the `.dark`
class (that's `themeMode`), so on the modern shell you'd get white surfaces +
dark legacy bits + amber accent — a mixed/broken state. Two overlapping dark
mechanisms confuse the model.

Options to brainstorm (needs a design decision, touches Display settings +
useTheme.js — do NOT bundle with Problem 1):
- selecting the "Dark"/"Light" theme sets the corresponding mode, OR
- drop Light/Dark as selectable themes entirely (the mode toggle covers them),
  leaving only expressive themes as selectable.

## Reference
- useTheme.js `applyCustomTheme()` (lines 59-96): `--<key>` loop + focus special-casing.
- theme.css: legacy tokens (~4-28 / .dark 133-159) vs redesign tokens (30-49 / .dark 161-176).
- builtin.json: the 5 built-ins.

title: Docker dev backend writes root-owned files into backend/data, breaking host-run backend
description: calvin-backend-dev runs as root and bind-mounts the repo, so plugin installs from the container create root-owned dirs under backend/data/plugins/. Options: run the container with user: 1000:100, or move container data off the bind mount. Also note both backends (host :8002, docker :8001) share the same SQLite DB and data dir — in-memory plugin registries drift apart until restart.

comments.author: Simon Österberg
comments.text: Fixed: root cause was a singular/plural env-var mismatch — setting is plugins_dir (reads PLUGINS_DIR) but all deploy configs set PLUGIN_DIR, so it was silently ignored and installs fell back to ./data/plugins in the bind-mounted repo (root-owned -> host backend Errno 13). Added AliasChoices('plugins_dir','plugin_dir') so PLUGIN_DIR is honored with zero deploy churn; container now installs to the /var/lib/calvin volume, host keeps ./data/plugins, no more collision. title: Model rolling as a windowing modifier (base view × rolling), add rolling-week
description:
Rolling is currently a 4th value of the single `calendarViewMode` field (month/week/day/rolling), which makes it mutually exclusive with the base views and asymmetric in the on-calendar toggle (you can cycle *out* of rolling to month, but not *into* it). Rolling isn't a peer view — it's a windowing choice orthogonal to granularity.

## Model
Two independent axes:
- Base granularity (the on-calendar toggle): Month / Week / Day
- Windowing (a Settings behavior): Fixed calendar period vs. Rolling window anchored to now

'Rolling' = roll the next unit down:
- Month + rolling → rolls WEEKS (N weeks from the current week) = today's existing rolling behavior
- Week + rolling → rolls DAYS (next N days from today) = NEW 'rolling week' render path
- Day + rolling → n/a

## Work
- Split `calendarViewMode` into base view (month/week/day) + a `rollingWindow` on/off flag (reuse the existing `calendarWeeks` count; add a days count for rolling-week). Keep back-compat: legacy 'rolling' value maps to base=month + rollingWindow=on.
- Keep the on-calendar toggle strictly Month/Week/Day; expose rolling on/off + count in Settings → Content → Calendar display (ContentSettings.vue).
- Implement rolling-week: N days starting today. NOTE design decision: rolling days break fixed Mon–Sun weekday columns (today lands in column 1), so headers become per-day dates — effectively a 'next N days' agenda strip rather than a weekday grid. Decide deliberately.
- Update CalendarView.vue calendarDays/loadEvents/navigation/currentMonthYear/isCurrentPeriod to key off (base, rolling) instead of the 4-value field.

## Context
Follow-up from the calendar header/fullscreen/rolling-fix work (calvin-00s). The overlap-cache bug that made rolling drop events on navigation was already fixed separately in plugin_calendar_service (full-coverage instead of >=50% overlap).

description:

that focuses a region (calendar event, service, photo) re-reveals the UI.

Desired: let users interact with content while the UI stays hidden. Reveal the
UI only via a deliberate affordance — a hot corner (e.g. the existing
MinimalUIOverlay reveal button, possibly enlarged into a corner hit-target),
or a specific gesture. Make tap-anywhere-reveal optional (a setting) since
some users may prefer it.

- frontend/src/components/MinimalUIOverlay.vue — existing bottom-left reveal button

title: Global 'Corner style' setting: user-configurable radius scale
description:
Add a global, user-configurable corner-roundness control, mirroring the Settings UI size pattern. Purely cosmetic personalization axis.

MECHANISM: a --radius-scale multiplier baked into the existing radius tokens in frontend/src/styles/theme.css, e.g.
  --radius-xs: calc(6px * var(--radius-scale));  (and sm/md/lg/xl/2xl)
  --radius-pill stays FIXED (999px) — a pill is a pill.
Default --radius-scale = 1 => no-op (baseline unchanged). Discrete PRESETS (not a slider — arbitrary values look broken): e.g. Sharp 0 / Subtle 0.5 / Default 1 / Round 1.6. Stored as a string preset key 'cornerStyle' via /api/config (mirror uiSize plumbing: configRegistry.js + config.js + useConfigForm.js + backend config.py). Preset->factor map in a styles/ module like uiScale.js. Apply via a composable mirroring useUiScale (set --radius-scale on <html>, localStorage boot cache + config sync). UI: SegmentedControl in Settings -> Appearance next to 'Settings UI size'.

BLOCKED BY radius-token adoption — otherwise the knob rounds some elements and not others (whack-a-mole). Must land AFTER:
  - calvin-bvw (region editor adopts --radius-*)
  - calvin-0wr (service regions adopt --radius-*)
Also sweep any remaining hardcoded radii app-wide onto tokens before shipping (grep 'border-radius:.*px' outside theme.css).

OPEN DESIGN Q: standalone global control (recommended, parallels UI size, direct user control) vs. folding radius into the theme layer (each theme defines roundness; keeps appearance model unified). Decide before building.

DONE = one preset control visibly restyles corners consistently across settings + dashboard + plugins; Default is a pixel no-op; pills unaffected.

title: Per-region calendar display overrides in the tune popover (week numbers, event density)
description:
Extend the calendar tune button (RegionViewOptions / CalendarViewOptions, from calvin-bc5) to carry per-region DISPLAY settings as overrides of the global defaults. Design agreed with user 2026-07-03.

SCOPE — settings to move (as per-region overrides):
- Week numbers (global: config.showWeekNumbers)
- Event density / max visible events (global: config.maxVisibleEvents)
DO NOT move: weekStartDay, weekendDays (locale/personal — stay global in Settings), showRedDays (deferred placeholder; isRedDay() returns false).

MODEL — per-region override of a global default (tri-state), NOT a flat move:
- Global Settings keeps the baseline value (unchanged).
- The region 'view' object gains OPTIONAL fields. Absent = inherit the global value, so there is NO data migration for existing regions.
  - CalendarView reads: showWeekNumbers -> props.view?.weekNumbers ?? configStore.showWeekNumbers
  - and maxVisible -> props.view?.maxVisibleEvents ?? configStore.maxVisibleEvents
- Week numbers UI = tri-state segmented control (Default / On / Off). 'Default' persists as undefined/null (or a 'default' sentinel) so it keeps tracking the global.
- Event density UI = a stepper like the existing Weeks/Days stepper, but with a 'Default' affordance (e.g. a Default chip that clears the override back to inherit). Clamp 1–20 to match config setMaxVisibleEvents.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
- Shape/clamp: extend DEFAULT_CALENDAR_VIEW + clampCalendarView in frontend/src/utils/layout.js. Keep new fields optional; clamp only when present (preserve undefined = inherit). Watch the reactive-proxy JSON-clone in setRegionView (see commit 6bd05e7).
- Persist via configStore.updateRegionView(regionId, patch) (same path the tune popover already uses). Setting back to Default should delete the key (patch with undefined) or store a 'default' sentinel — pick one and handle in clamp.
- CalendarView.vue: replace the three global reads (showWeekNumbers, maxVisibleEvents; getVisibleEvents/getOverflowCount use maxVisibleEvents) with view-aware computeds that fall back to global.
- CalendarViewOptions.vue: add the two rows. Consider a small tri-state segmented component (Default/On/Off) — may be reusable; check if one exists before writing a new one.
- Tests: extend CalendarViewOptions.spec + CalendarViewMonth/Rolling or a new spec — assert inherit-from-global when unset, override when set, and that 'Default' clears back to inherit.

Optional follow-on: this same override pattern is what service regions would use via calvin-39g (RegionViewOptions reuse).

STATUS 2026-07-03: Implemented on feat/per-region-calendar-display (commit 09a0313, pushed). Week numbers = compact tri-state Default/On/Off; events/day = stepper + Default reset chip (month only). clampCalendarView keeps weekNumbers (bool) + maxVisibleEvents (1-20) as optional fields, omitted when absent (inherit, no migration). CalendarView reads view ?? global. 834 frontend unit tests pass; lint+prettier clean; verified visually light+dark. PENDING: PR/merge to develop.

title: Mealie recipe links: return-to-Calvin path or render recipe in-app
description:
Mealie plugin recipe cards are clickable links (desirable — we want them clickable), but opening a recipe navigates away / into another tab with no way back to Calvin. On a kiosk dashboard this strands the user.

Decide between two approaches:
(a) Keep the outbound link but provide a return-to-Calvin affordance (e.g. a back control, or open in an in-app frame/overlay with a close button) when a recipe opens.
(b) Parse the Mealie API and render the recipe inside Calvin ourselves (own detail view), so we never leave the app.

Design decision needed before implementation. Reported by user.

title: Reconcile orientation (portrait/landscape) with the region builder
description: User 2026-06-30 question: 'Switch to portrait/landscape' doesn't make much sense alongside the region builder. title: Regions editor: design-cohesion pass — compose ui/ primitives, unify radius/spacing
description:

Design review (2026-07-04) found the editor is 'out of dialect' with the rest of the Display settings page: it reimplements controls inline (4/6px radius, sub-44px targets, native OS selects, a hand-rolled toggle, bare number input) instead of composing the app's ui/ primitives that every sibling row uses. Vocabulary (unicode glyphs, muted-ink intros) is already idiomatic — this is conform-to-primitives, not a redesign.

Scope:
1. Swap native/custom controls for ui/ primitives:
   - clock-bar mode/position native <select> -> SelectPill (mode is 2-option, consider SegmentedControl like Orientation)
   - .clock-bar-switch hand-rolled toggle -> ToggleSwitch
   - region size <input type=number> -> NumberStepper
   - component picker menu -> align with ActionPicker searchable-picker styling (8px radius, 44px rows)
2. Unify radius: retire hardcoded 4/6px for the app's de-facto 8px(tiles)/11px(pills)/16px(panels) convention (no radius tokens exist).
3. Ensure 44px touch targets on icon buttons (x delete, collapse chevron are ~25-30px now).
4. Break the cramped screen-header toolbar into breathing room (name-row + action-cluster, or use SettingRow stacked mode). Relates to now-closed calvin-3v4 (header crowding).
5. Dial back accent: the solid-blue full-width 'Clock bar' drag token is the loudest thing on a page where accent otherwise only marks selection — make it a quiet chip; reserve solid --focus for active screen/region.

KEEP: the WYSIWYG preview canvas (live resize handles, orientation-aware split) is the editor's signature — make chrome recede, keep the preview distinctive. Primitives live in frontend/src/components/ui/ (SelectPill, ToggleSwitch, SegmentedControl, NumberStepper). Reference sibling: keyboard editor (settings/tabs/layout/keyboard/, calvin-1bp).
close_reason: Complete — merged to develop via PR #70 (7a8ca17) + PR #69. Full regions-editor cohesion pass done: (1-4) clock-bar row + region controls → shell primitives, radii/spacing/font tokenized; drag-first simplification (dropped redundant position/orientation/size controls); region-kind accent + on-accent color tokens; (5) all glyph buttons → ui/IconButton (calvin-b97), redundant Activate control removed (switching lives on ScreenDots), screen header de-crowded into identity/actions groups, direction toggles got a proper DirectionSplitIcon (replacing ▭▭/▯|▯ glyphs).
